0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 1'11 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 January 1982, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council.
which covers chemical analysis of different ferro0.2 IS : 155%1961* namely, ferrosilicon, ferrochromium, ferromanganese and alloys, silicomanqanese, ferromolybdenum, ferrophosphorus, spcigrleisen, ferrotitanium, ferrovanadium and ferrotungsten, was first published in 1961. While reviewing this standard, the Sectional Committee felt that the Ftandard should be revised to cover ferrosilicon, and methods of analysis of other ferro-alloys should be covered in separate standards. During preparation of the revision of IS : 1559-1961*; it was felt convenient to cover methods of chemical analysis of ferrosilicon in different parts of the c;tandard \vhich on p,lblication would supersede Section 1 Ferrosilicon The committee also decided to rewrite the methods of IS : 1.75%1961*. taking into consideration the latest composition specified in IS : 1110. Though calcium and manganese are not specified in IS : 11 lo19s1t. 1081t, the determination of these elements is covered in this standard because these are generally required from the view point of determining for determining other elements in -interference of analysis in methods ferrosilicon due to presence of these elements. Moreover the determination of these elements may be required for comprehensive analysis of ferroiiliron. This part covers the determination of manganese. 5.8 Standard Sodium Arsenite Solution ( &025 N ) - Prapare the sodium arsenite solution by dissolving exactly around 1.23 g arsenious oxide ( AR ) in a solution of 10 g of sodium hydroxide ( AR ) in 30 ml of water, warming if necessary. Dilute to about 500 ml, neutralise by the addition of hydrochloric acid ( 1 N ) to phenolphthalein end point and then add 10 g of sodium bicarbonate ( AR ). Dilute to 1 litre in a volumetric flask. 5.8.1 To standardise the solution take exactly 10 ml of potassium permanganate solution ( 0.025 N ) by means of a pipette into 500-ml Add, about 5 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid ( see 5.9 ) beaker. and boil to reduce permanganate. Add about 10 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid ( see 5.10 ) down the sides of the beaker and take the solution to fumes. Cool, dilute to about 100 ml and titrate the manganese after persulphate oxidation as described in the procedure. Alternatively, the sample of ferrosilicon 5.9 Concentrated IS : 265-1976* ). 5.10 Concentrated IS : 266-19777) . 6. PROCEDURE 6.1 Weigh exactly around 1 g of the dried sample in a 50-ml tall form Add about 20 ml of hydrofluoric acid and platinum crucible. acid dropwise until the vigorous cautiously add concentrated nitric reaction has subsided. 6.2 Add 2 ml of dilute sulphuric acid and evaporate to fumes of sulphur trioxide. Cool the crucible, add 25 ml of water and transfer the contents to 250-ml beaker. Cool and make up to 250 ml in a volumetric flask. *Specification for hydrochloric acid ( secondrevision ). Keep the solution on a To the boiling solution, add about 5 ml of silver hot-plate and boil. nitrate solution and 10 ml of ammonium persulphate solution. Boil the contents briskly for about 2 minutes. Cool rapidly to room temperature and add 5 ml of sodium chloride solution. Titrate immediately with standard sodium arsenite solution to a colourless end point.
6.4 Carry out a blank determination following the same procedure and using the same amount of all reagents and correct the final result for the blank value, if any.
